transcript.text: I think my washer dryer has a fault - I put it on just a drying programme with dry-ish clothes and I can hear water running into it and draining the whole time. Surely it shouldn't use water to dry? It's a Beko.

It sounds like your washer-dryer is behaving normally. Most Beko condenser dryer models use a trickle of cold water during the drying cycle to cool down the heat exchanger, which allows the moisture in the clothes to turn into water and drain away. This explains why you hear water running and draining even though you are only drying. However, if the clothes are coming out damp at the end, it is usually due to airflow or load size rather than a broken part. Please check: 1) Was the load small enough for drying (typically half the wash capacity)? 2) Is the lint filter (usually behind a flap at the bottom front) clean?
Thank you. My clothes actually come out dry, so nothing is failing as such. I just wanted to be sure the trickling water is normal and not a fault. Is that right?

Yes, that is exactly right. Since your clothes are coming out dry, the water running and draining during the cycle is completely normal for a Beko condenser washer-dryer. The machine uses cold water to cool down its internal heat exchanger so it can condense moisture from the clothes into liquid water, which then drains away. As long as the drying performance is good, there is no fault.

candidates: Normal condensation process (cold water used for cooling) (high)
Restricted airflow or blocked filter causing poor drying efficiency (medium)
Overloaded drum for the dry cycle capacity (medium)
